question: An investigator is studying the crossbridge cycle of muscle contraction. Tissue from the biceps brachii muscle is obtained at the autopsy of an 87-year-old man. Investigation of the muscle tissue shows myosin heads attached to actin filaments. Binding of myosin heads to which of the following elements would most likely cause detachment of myosin from actin filaments?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Myosin heads attached to actin filaments" -> "Detachment of myosin from actin filaments" -> "Requires energy" -> "ATP" -> 95% CHAIN: "Myosin heads attached to actin filaments" -> "Detachment of myosin from actin filaments" -> "Release of inorganic phosphate" -> "ADP" -> 95%
analysis: In the crossbridge cycle of muscle contraction, detachment of myosin from actin filaments is primarily triggered by the binding of ATP to the myosin head, leading to the release of the myosin head from actin. ATP hydrolysis then allows the myosin head to re-energize and reattach to actin for the next cycle of contraction.
